articles.title: Amata CEO Vikrom Kromadit built his industrial park empire in Thailand and Vietnam. Laos is next - Fortune
articles.summary: Amata CEO Vikrom Kromadit built his industrial park empire in Thailand and Vietnam. Laos is next  Fortune
articles.full_text:
Thai real estate developer Amata Corporation says Laos will become its “largest focus” in the years to come, CEO Vikrom Kromadit tells Fortune.
“Laos will become our largest focus because of the land bank that they have,” Kromadit tells Fortune. “They also have lots of green energy—that’s why they’re called the battery of Southeast Asia.”
Amata expanded into Laos in 2022, starting with Amata City Namor, which covers 31.5 square kilometers and sits beside a station on the China-Laos Railway. The company says its long-term Laos vision could reach 200 square kilometers.
Kromadit’s company built its fortunes in Thailand and Vietnam. Amata Corporation, founded in 1989, built industrial parks across Thailand’s Rayong and Chon Buri provinces. It was also an early backer of Vietnam, building its first facility there in 1994, early in the Southeast Asian country’s reform program. Laos, however, offers an opportunity for Amata to capture Chinese manufacturers expanding to new manufacturing hubs in Southeast Asia.
Laos, Southeast Asia’s only landlocked country, boasts a huge energy surplus, as its rivers and mountainous terrain supported a government-led push to build hydroelectric dams as a core economic pillar. The country currently exports about 80% of its electricity to other Asian countries like Thailand, China, and Singapore.
“They have plenty of land and a lot of water,” Kromadit says, adding that it has “the best natural conditions” for industrial development. (While Laos generates over 12 GW of capacity from over 80 hydro plants, most cross-border transmission lines bypass local communities, sticking consumers with frequent blackouts.)
To Kromadit, Laos’s potential is also backed by China, long the country’s top foreign investor. In 2025, China pumped $18 billion into Laos’s economy, primarily toward industry, mining, and agriculture, according to the Vientiane Times, a local newspaper.
Laos has been slotted into “China plus one” supply chains, where both Chinese and global manufacturers move some—or all—of their production to other countries, both to reduce cost and avoid tariffs on Chinese-origin products.
“China is the largest manufacturer of all products, so they can’t just keep building only within their country,” Kromadit explains. “They’re also being hit by political pressure from the U.S.”
After graduating from National Taiwan University with a degree in mechanical engineering, he returned to Thailand in 1975 and founded V&K Enterprise, an import-export business that focused on agricultural products, minerals, and seafood. But by the 1980s, he was frustrated with being “just a middleman.”
“I wanted to make more money,” Kromadit confesses. “When I was in the food business, even though I was the one who created all the channels and brought in business, once companies achieved success, they kicked me out.”
In 1988, he cofounded the Bang Pakong Industrial Estate on the eastern coast of Bangkok, then established Amata Corporation in 1989. Amata’s first industrial facility, Amata City Chon Buri, opened that same year.
After Kromadit visited Vietnam in 1990, he decided to make the country Amata’s first overseas market. “I found that the Vietnamese were focused, capable, and smart,” he says. “I thought that Vietnam, in the future, would compete with Thailand for industrial investments.” Amata launched Amata City Bien Hoa in Dong Nai province in 1994.
His prediction has largely come true: Vietnam is now Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing economy, with Q3 GDP growth of 9.95%. Hanoi wants to have Vietnam reach high-income status by 2045.
Amata today hosts more than 1,500 factories in 12 locations across Thailand, Vietnam, and Laos. It briefly attempted an expansion into Myanmar in 2019, with a facility in Yangon, the country’s commercial center. Plans were halted in early 2021 following a military coup and resulting civil war.
Amata positions its facilities as industrial cities that include not just factories but also housing, schools, hospitals, and shopping malls. The company’s flagship Chon Buri campus, for instance, houses the massive 38,000-square-meter Lotus Plus Mall, which includes a hypermarket, retail stores, banks, restaurants, and an international cinema.
The company’s facilities include kindergartens, schools, and technical training institutes, with more on the way. “We’re now looking to build a university,” Kromadit says.
Asked whether Amata might expand into other Southeast Asian markets, like Indonesia or Cambodia, Kromadit says the company already has enough land to occupy him for the rest of his life.
“The land that we have on hand is around 700 square kilometers,” he says. “It’s big enough to make me busy until I go to heaven.”

articles.title: Singapore to prioritise ASEAN digital trade initiatives: PM Wong - Singapore Business Review
articles.summary: Singapore to prioritise ASEAN digital trade initiatives: PM Wong  Singapore Business Review
articles.full_text:
The measures fall under the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement.
Singapore will look to prioritise ASEAN digital trade initiatives when it assumes the bloc's chairmanship next year, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said.
The initiatives fall under the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement, which aims to reduce regulatory barriers, facilitate cross-border data flows, and improve digital trade across the region.
Speaking at the DBS Asia Future Forward Conference on 12 October, Wong said firms operating across the region currently face differing regulations, systems, and requirements.
The agreement aims to enable companies to reach customers across the region more easily, conduct cross-border payments with less friction and potentially lower costs, and expand their operations across ASEAN.
However, Wong pointed out that more work must be done to translate DEFA into practical benefits for companies.
“When Singapore takes on the chair of ASEAN, we will look at how we can give some priority to some of these initiatives," he added.
Wong identified market fragmentation as a challenge for Southeast Asian startups seeking to scale their operations and attract investment.
He said greater economic integration, alongside stronger entrepreneurship and innovation ecosystems, could help support the development of larger capital markets in the region.

articles.title: S’pore to deepen ASEAN integration, global trade ties in 2027 - Singapore Business Review
articles.summary: S’pore to deepen ASEAN integration, global trade ties in 2027  Singapore Business Review
articles.full_text:
It is eyeing stronger connections with Latin America, Africa, and the Middle East.
Singapore plans to deepen economic integration within ASEAN and expand its global trade connections when it assumes the bloc's chairmanship in 2027, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said.
The Republic will strengthen ties with existing partners whilst exploring opportunities in new regions, including Latin America, Africa, and the Middle East.
"We will do so with Southeast Asia and accelerate the integration in ASEAN," Wong said at the 24th Forbes Global CEO Conference on 8 October.
The move comes as Wong said countries are increasingly introducing trade restrictions to protect domestic industries and jobs.
“We see more trade, but the global economy will become more fragmented and fragmented by regions. In such an environment, what can Singapore do?” he added.
He further pointed out that trade remains three times Singapore's GDP, making it necessary for the country to maintain and diversify its international connections.
"Our strategy is to deepen and diversify our connections," Wong said.
Wong added that Singapore would continue to remain open to trade and investment as global economic conditions become more unpredictable.

articles.title: Malaysia education minister defends day-to-day decisions on haze-related school closures - CNA
articles.summary: Malaysia education minister defends day-to-day decisions on haze-related school closures  CNAMalaysia to raise transboundary haze issue at ASEAN meeting, says existing disaster mechanisms do not cover it  CNAFootball games, night markets carry on in Johor amid haze and school closures  The Straits Times‘When there is no smoke, we send oxygen’ – Indonesian government communications chief  Sinar DailyTransboundary haze law must take into consideration many f...
articles.full_text:
Some parents have suggested closing schools for several consecutive days to make it easier for families to make arrangements, said Malaysia Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek.
SINGAPORE: Malaysia's education minister on Monday (Oct 12) defended its day-to-day approach to school closures, as parents called for more certainty over arrangements during the worsening haze.
In a Facebook post, Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said some parents had suggested closing schools for several consecutive days to make it easier for families to plan ahead.
But decisions have to take into account fluctuating air quality and the disruption that prolonged closures could cause to students’ learning, she said.
“In making decisions, it is important to understand the air pollutant index (API) readings can change depending on time and location,” she said.
School closures must therefore take into account the prevailing conditions in each area, she added.
“I understand these concerns. That’s why I have requested that decisions on school closures be announced as early as possible to give parents time to prepare,” said Fadhlina.
Haze management also involves several agencies, she explained, with the environment department responsible for monitoring air quality and addressing pollution while the health ministry provides the public with guidance on health risks.
The education ministry, meanwhile, focuses on students’ safety and the management of school operations based on prevailing conditions, she said.
Fadhlina also pointed to the impact of prolonged school disruptions during the COVID-19 pandemic.
“Until today, efforts to address learning loss (during COVID-19) are still ongoing. Lost learning time is not easily recovered, especially since access to home-based teaching and learning facilities is not the same for all students,” she said.
For boarding school students, the ministry’s recommendation is that they remain in their hostels during haze-related school closures as long as the conditions are safe.
“The education ministry does not want parents to be burdened with repeatedly picking up and sending their children back to school,” Fadhlina said.
Malaysia has 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide under its Environmental Quality Monitoring Programme.
Under the education ministry’s guidelines, schools in areas with API readings above 180 must close. Schools will also close if readings remain above 150 for three consecutive days.
The worsening haze has prompted school closures in several states across Peninsular Malaysia since last week, with announcements made a day before.
Schools in Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang, Putrajaya alongside parts of Kuala Lumpur and Selangor resumed in-person classes on Monday after API readings on Sunday improved to moderate levels, local media reported.
In Johor, however, which remains the worst-affected state, all schools and educational institutions will remain closed for another five days from Oct 12 to Oct 16.
Johor began closing schools on Thursday. Several other affected states and areas followed suit on Friday.
The education ministry has said that state authorities will decide on school closures based on haze conditions, according to local media.

articles.title: FM Sitharaman meets global financial leaders in Singapore, discusses India investment opportunities - Malaysia Sun
articles.summary: FM Sitharaman meets global financial leaders in Singapore, discusses India investment opportunities  Malaysia Sun
articles.full_text:
ANI
                
12 Oct 2026, 09:01 GMT+10
            
Singapore, October 12 (ANI): Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman held meetings with senior executives of five global financial institutions and investment firms in Singapore to discuss expanding their engagement in India across infrastructure financing, private credit, artificial intelligence (AI), renewable energy and housing finance.
According to posts shared by the Ministry of Finance on X, the meetings involved representatives from Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC), Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken (SEB), HPS Investment Partners, B Capital Group and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG).
During her meeting with HPS Investment Partners CEO Scott Kapnick, Sitharaman discussed "private credit, structured finance and long-term financing for businesses".
The ministry's post said she encouraged HPS to explore setting up a fund in GIFT IFSC and collaboration with the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) to "mobilise financing for large infrastructure projects in India".
"HPS highlighted the potential to leverage debt capital to complement equity investments," the ministry said.
In talks with MUFG Chief Executive for Asia Pacific Yukinobu Saeki, discussions focused on expanding the bank's presence in India, particularly in "capital markets, infrastructure and project finance, renewable energy and M&A financing".
Sitharaman also encouraged greater engagement with the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) to support infrastructure financing. The meeting covered financing support for Indian small and medium enterprises and regulatory roadshows to "enhance market transparency and governance".
During her meeting with SEB Chairperson Marcus Wallenberg, discussions covered India's economic outlook and ways to strengthen investment flows from European institutional investors. The SEB team highlighted opportunities across "energy and data centres, IT and tax services, healthcare, financial services and housing finance".
The talks also covered sustainable finance, private equity investments in non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), the green transition and skill development.
Sitharaman also met SMBC Managing Executive Officer and Co-Head for Asia Pacific Rajeev Kannan to discuss opportunities to expand the bank's engagement in India, including "affordable housing finance, financing for NBFCs, trade finance and other priority sectors".
She encouraged the bank to explore investment and financing opportunities through NIIF and GIFT IFSC, particularly in aircraft leasing.
Separately, discussions with B Capital Group Co-founder and CEO Raj Ganguly focused on "Sovereign AI and the broader AI ecosystem". Sitharaman highlighted India's potential to emerge as a leader in AI services and encouraged the firm to explore AI applications in banking and financial services.
The ministry said B Capital emphasised the importance of a "stable currency and predictable, transparent tax policies" for investors.
The discussions covered potential avenues to expand financing for Indian businesses and infrastructure and attract investment across technology, energy and other sectors. (ANI)

articles.title: Exports target $1 trillion: Where does the growth come from? - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Exports target $1 trillion: Where does the growth come from?  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
TPO - The Ministry of Industry and Trade is developing a strategy for import and export of goods until 2030, with scenarios setting three targets: high, medium, and low growth. Under the high growth target, export turnover will exceed 1 trillion USD.
Proposal to raise export growth target by nearly three times.
According to the draft Strategy for Goods Export and Import until 2030, with a vision to 2045, developed by the Ministry of Industry and Trade , the target for export growth in the 2026-2030 period is an average of 15-16% per year, while import growth is 12-13% per year.
Notably, this export growth rate is nearly three times higher than the average target of 5-6% per year for the 2026-2030 period in the strategy approved by the Prime Minister in 2022.
According to the Ministry of Industry and Trade, the draft proposes three export scenarios up to 2030, including a scenario with a low growth target.$765 billion, with an average growth of $953.7 billion and a peak of $1,041 billion.
The draft also aims to maintain an average export surplus of 3-6%; increase the export share of domestic enterprises to 28-30% by 2030 and 38-40% by 2045.
Furthermore, the proportion of processed and refined goods is expected to reach 89-90% of total export turnover; high-tech products will account for approximately 50% of the value of processed and manufactured goods exports by 2030.
You may also like
According to the Customs Department, in 2025, Vietnam's goods exports will reach US$475 billion, an increase of 17% compared to the previous year. Of this, the processed industrial sector will account for 88.7% of the total export value, followed by agricultural, forestry, and aquatic products.
Notably, electronics, computers, and components led with $107.7 billion; machinery and equipment reached $59 billion; and telephones and components reached $56.7 billion.
Proposal to shift strongly towards deep processing.
Speaking to Tien Phong newspaper, Mr. Nguyen Quoc Khanh, Chairman of the Vietnam Wood and Forest Products Association, said that the export value of the wood industry has increased from approximately 300 million USD 20 years ago to 17.2 billion USD in 2025. However, many businesses still lack mastery in product design, development, and branding, which create high added value.
Representatives from the Vietnam Wood and Forest Products Association proposed strengthening links with FDI enterprises to access technology and expand markets, thereby enhancing the capacity of Vietnamese businesses.
Sharing the same view, Mr. Thai Nhu Hiep, Vice President of the Vietnam Coffee and Cocoa Association, believes that linkages between businesses are still limited. Many small businesses still sell their products through FDI companies, while large businesses trade through international traders.
According to Mr. Hiep, the coffee industry needs to strengthen linkages between businesses, raw material areas, and processing and product development activities to increase export value.
You may also like
Representatives from the Vietnam Food Association (VFA) suggested focusing on building a national rice brand, learning from Thailand 's experience in developing the Hom Mali rice brand, while also diversifying export markets, improving quality, and ensuring that rice farmers benefit from increased product value.
Speaking at a recent conference on export strategy consultation, Mr. Nguyen Hoai Nam, General Secretary of the Vietnam Association of Seafood Processing and Export (VASEP), stated that the strategy needs to clearly define objectives, resources, roadmap, and responsibilities for implementation. Tasks should be concretized into action programs, with coordination among ministries, sectors, and localities.
According to Mr. Nam, increasing export value must be linked to removing obstacles related to raw materials, improving management mechanisms, and facilitating processing activities. Some inappropriate regulations may affect businesses' ability to access raw materials and fulfill orders.
Mr. Pham Van Quan, Deputy Director of the Industry Department, Ministry of Industry and Trade, suggested focusing on developing supporting industries and creating conditions for domestic enterprises to participate more deeply in global supply chains, especially in the electronics and automotive sectors.

articles.title: US lifts sanctions on daughter of Myanmar military-linked businessman - The Star
articles.summary: US lifts sanctions on daughter of Myanmar military-linked businessman  The Star
articles.full_text:
WASHINGTON (Reuters): The United States lifted on Friday sanctions on the daughter of a Myanmar businessman accused of supporting the country's military, according to the US Treasury Department's website, after she filed a suit seeking removal from the blacklist.
The move comes after Reuters reported this week that the Trump administration had opened talks with Myanmar's military-installed government, reversing US policy that sought to isolate the generals who overthrew elected leaders in 2021.
A State Department spokesperson said the decision to remove Myanmar national Theint Win Htet from the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List) "reflects the administration’s determination that this designation no longer effectively supports US policy objectives related to Burma."
"The administration is using a range of tools to advance key priorities regarding Burma, such as combating scam centers, improving Burma's domestic operating environment for US businesses, and encouraging a peace process to address the ongoing violence and humanitarian crisis," the spokesperson said, using the country's previous name.
After the 2021 coup, former President Joe Biden's administration imposed sanctions on senior Myanmar military officers and companies it accused of providing support for the military junta, which triggered a nationwide civil war that has killed an estimated 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million.
The Treasury in January 2024 targeted the Shwe Byain Phyu Group of Companies, its founder Thein Win Zaw and his family, saying the company imported and distributed petroleum on behalf of the military and that the family owned at least 20 companies closely associated with the regime.
Thein Win Zaw's adult daughter, Theint Win Htet, sued the Biden administration seeking her removal from the SDN List, but her case was dismissed in February 2025. The sanctions freeze any US assets of those targeted and generally bar Americans from dealing with them.
The US in July 2025 lifted sanctions on several other Myanmar nationals and a firm under sanctions for aiding the military.
Theint Win Htet filed a new complaint in July this year, arguing that she has no active role in her father's business affairs, adding that the sanctions had interrupted her studies in the US, where she completed a bachelor's degree at New York University and was enrolled in a master's program at Columbia University.
"Plaintiff’s US credit cards have been blocked, her foreign bank accounts have been restricted, closed, or refused, and she has been unable to complete her university studies in the United States," said the complaint by Theint Win Htet, who said in the complaint she now lives with her mother in Bangkok. Her mother was removed from the sanctions list last year.
Campaign group Justice For Myanmar denounced the US move at a time when it said the Myanmar military was escalating attacks on civilians. "It is deplorable that the US government continues to delist Myanmar cronies and their family members that provide funding for the junta's terror," the group said.
Theint Win Htet's lawyer, Washington-based sanctions specialist Erich Ferrari, filed a notice with the US District Court for the District of Columbia on Friday voluntarily dismissing the lawsuit after her delisting. Ferrari declined to comment.
(Reporting by Simon Lewis and Michelle Nichols; Editing by Daphne Psaledakis, Sanjeev Miglani and Andrea Ricci) -- Reuters

articles.title: Thai Nguyen: Attracting high-quality FDI to create momentum for realizing double-digit growth targets. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Thai Nguyen: Attracting high-quality FDI to create momentum for realizing double-digit growth targets.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
With positive results in attracting foreign direct investment (FDI), along with the orientation towards developing industrial infrastructure, improving the quality of human resources, and promoting administrative reform, Thai Nguyen province is gradually building an important foundation to realize the goal of double-digit economic growth.
FDI continues to affirm its role as a driver of growth.
In the first nine months of 2026, Thai Nguyen recorded positive results in attracting foreign direct investment (FDI), with a total newly registered and increased capital of US$8,052.9 million. This included 23 newly licensed FDI projects with a total registered capital of US$5,811.05 million; and 22 projects with adjusted capital increases, adding US$2,241.85 million. As of September 30, 2026, the province had a cumulative total of 251 FDI projects with a total registered capital of US$19.406 billion.
The above figures demonstrate Thai Nguyen's attractiveness to international investors and reflect the trend of expanding production and business activities of enterprises already present in the locality. Capital continues to flow into the fields of electronics, component and circuit board manufacturing, processing and manufacturing industries, and high technology, creating momentum to promote the shift in economic structure towards industrialization and modernization.
Khám phá thêm
Tìm hiểu lịch sử
Đọc Mẹo Du Lịch
Khám phá ĐNA
For achieving double-digit growth targets, FDI is crucial in many aspects. Firstly, attracting large-scale projects contributes to supplementing investment resources, expanding industrial production capacity, and increasing export value. Once these projects become operational, the demand for labor, logistics services, transportation, trade, and supporting industries also increases, creating a ripple effect on the local economy.
Furthermore, the continued increase in capital by existing investors demonstrates the potential for expanding production and maintaining the competitiveness of the investment environment. This provides a basis for Thai Nguyen to consolidate its growth momentum in the medium and long term, instead of relying solely on attracting new projects.
However, for FDI to truly become a driving force for rapid and sustainable growth, it requires not only an increase in the scale of registered capital, but also improvements in the quality of disbursement, production efficiency, budget contributions, job quality, and connectivity between FDI enterprises and domestic businesses.
One of the highlights in Thai Nguyen's investment attraction strategy is the development of electronics, semiconductor, and high-tech projects in the Yen Binh Industrial Park. Spanning 197.61 hectares and with a total investment exceeding 3,500 billion VND, the project is envisioned as a "Pioneering Urban Technology Complex," integrating hardware and software production with centers for finance, commerce and services, research and development (R&D), education and training, and housing for experts.
You may also like
This model opens up a new approach to industrial development, where production infrastructure is connected to an ecosystem of research, training, and support services. Through this, businesses can improve operational efficiency, access suitable human resources, and enhance their innovation capabilities.
This is also a significant step towards the province's goal of double-digit growth. Developing high-tech industries not only creates additional production capacity but also opens up opportunities to increase added value, improve labor productivity, and promote technology transfer. If implemented comprehensively, Thai Nguyen can gradually transform from a center for electronics manufacturing to a hub for the development of electronics, semiconductor industries, and research and development activities.
In reality, operations in industrial zones show that many businesses maintain high production capacity thanks to stable orders, while proactively diversifying their supply sources and enhancing their competitiveness in the face of fluctuations in the international market.
Ms. Tu Chi Yen, Deputy Director of Human Resources at RQ Technology Vietnam, stated: Thai Nguyen has the advantage of its geographical location and transportation system, especially the expressways, which help businesses connect conveniently with Hanoi , economic centers, and seaports. This contributes to saving time and logistics costs, improving operational efficiency, and strengthening business confidence. Therefore, businesses have decided to invest and develop long-term in the locality.
Creating room for sustainable growth.
Recognizing that the competition to attract FDI is increasingly shifting from incentives to the ability to meet investors' requirements, Mr. Nguyen The Hoan, Head of the Management Board of Industrial Parks in Thai Nguyen province, said: The locality is stepping up investment promotion in a professional and focused manner, strengthening coordination with central ministries and agencies, and expanding cooperation with international investment promotion organizations and business associations such as KORCHAM, KOTRA, JETRO, AmCham Vietnam, EuroCham, and the Taiwan Business Association in Vietnam.
In addition, the province focuses on improving industrial park infrastructure, transportation, electricity, logistics, and digital infrastructure. According to the plan, Thai Nguyen has 37 industrial parks with a total area of nearly 14,000 hectares, along with a concentrated information technology park of about 200 hectares. This is an important foundation for preparing land, technical infrastructure, and conditions to receive large-scale high-tech projects.
You may also like
High-quality human resources are also identified as a key factor. Strengthening the links between the State, schools, and businesses, prioritizing the training of human resources in the fields of semiconductors, electronics, artificial intelligence, data science , automation, and digital technology will contribute to meeting production needs while enhancing the participation of local labor in high value-added processes.
Simultaneously, administrative reform, digital transformation , expansion of online public services, and the implementation of a "green channel" mechanism for key projects continue to be necessary solutions to shorten processing times, reduce compliance costs, and enhance the transparency of the investment environment.
In the journey to realize double-digit economic growth, attracting high-quality FDI is one of the important drivers, but the ultimate effectiveness depends on the ability to transform capital flows into production capacity, technology, labor productivity, and real added value. With a focus on developing high-tech industries, investing in synchronized infrastructure, improving human resource quality, and enhancing the business environment, Thai Nguyen is gradually consolidating its foundation for faster, more sustainable growth and deeper participation in the global value chain.

articles.title: Thai actor questions 5,050 baht airport departure tax on flight - Thaiger
articles.summary: Thai actor questions 5,050 baht airport departure tax on flight  ThaigerThailand eyes US$30 departure tax for tourists in revenue push  The Business TimesThailand plans entry and exit fees totalling $338 for air travellers  The Standard (HK)Tourism firms baulk at allocation of arrival fee  Bangkok PostThai hotels warn of 20% ASEAN visitor drop, oppose travel tax  Khaosod English
articles.full_text:
A Thai actor has questioned a 5,050 baht charge labelled as an airport departure tax on a flight from Bangkok to Vientiane, Laos, raising concerns about rising travel costs and confusion over Thailand’s proposed new departure tax.
However, a breakdown of the booking suggests that the amount includes several airline surcharges and airport-related fees rather than a single government tax.
Thai actor Duke Phanudet Watnasuchart reportedly shared details of his December flight booking on social media on October 9, questioning why the additional charges were significantly higher than those for the same route in August.
Although the original post appears to have since been removed, several Thai media outlets reported on the complaint and reproduced details of his booking.
According to Thai media reports, Duke previously paid approximately 2,365 baht in combined taxes and fees. His latest booking showed a base airfare of 7,040 baht and another 5,050 baht labelled as Airport Departure Tax, bringing the total to 12,090 baht.
The post prompted speculation that the increase was linked to Thailand’s proposed 1,000 baht departure tax, which is currently under public consultation.
However, a detailed price breakdown published by Thai media showed that the 5,050 baht consisted of 2,650 baht in airline-imposed charges and 2,400 baht in airport taxes and other fees.
The airline charges included a 2,300 baht surcharge identified as YQAC and another 350 baht airline fee.
The remaining charges included Thailand’s 1,120 baht international passenger service charge, a separate 510 baht airport fee, a 650 baht border clearance charge and another 120 baht in passenger information and international travel processing fees.
Part of the cost reflects changes to Thailand’s airport charges. Airports of Thailand (AOT) increased its international passenger service charge from 730 baht to 1,120 baht on June 20.
The increase applies to international departures from six AOT-operated airports, including Suvarnabhumi, Don Mueang and Phuket.
However, as the increase was already in effect during Duke’s August trip, it does not fully explain the difference between his two bookings. Changes to airline surcharges or other ticket-specific fees may also have contributed.
Meanwhile, Thailand is considering a separate 1,000 baht departure tax for travellers of all nationalities leaving the country by air.
The Revenue Department opened public consultations on September 30, with feedback accepted until October 29. The proposal has not been approved, meaning the new tax is not included in Duke’s booking.
The Thai Hotels Association has opposed the proposed tax, warning that additional travel charges could discourage international visitors and affect Thailand’s tourism competitiveness.
For foreign travellers, the case highlights the importance of reviewing ticket price breakdowns, as charges labelled as airport taxes may also include airline-imposed surcharges and other fees.

articles.title: Property prices fell by as much as 20% in the third quarter. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Property prices fell by as much as 20% in the third quarter.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
According to DXS-FERI, housing sales in the third quarter of 2026 decreased by 36% compared to the same period last year, despite price reductions of 5-20% in many segments compared to the previous quarter. Weak purchasing power led developers to increase discounts, extend payment terms, and offer interest rate support to attract customers.
According to the Vietnam Real Estate Market Report for the first nine months and forecast for the fourth quarter of 2026 by Dat Xanh Services Economic , Financial and Real Estate Research Institute (DXS-FERI), the housing market is undergoing adjustments in both selling prices and transactions. High loan interest rates, cautious credit policies, and the hesitant sentiment of buyers are factors affecting purchasing power.
Khám phá thêm
Tìm hiểu lịch sử
Đọc Mẹo Du Lịch
Khám phá ĐNA
In the third quarter of 2026, approximately 12,357 new housing units were launched nationwide, a 40% decrease compared to the previous quarter and a 54% decrease compared to the same period in 2025. The North accounted for 40% and the South for 36% of the new supply.
Despite a decrease in new supply in the third quarter, the total number of new housing units in the first three quarters of the year still reached approximately 49,657, a 33% increase compared to the same period last year. The majority came from large-scale urban developments by Vinhomes, Sun Group , Masterise Homes, and Ecopark.
Including both new products and products from previously launched projects still being offered by developers, the total primary supply in the first nine months reached approximately 114,857 units, a 21% increase compared to the same period last year. According to the report, the North accounted for about 48,333 units; the South had 37,592 units, mainly concentrated in Ho Chi Minh City and Dong Nai City; and the Central region had about 19,232 units.
Contrary to the increase in supply during the first nine months, housing sales decreased. The total number of units sold in the primary market reached approximately 32,469, a 16% decrease compared to the same period in 2025. In the third quarter alone, sales were estimated at 6,368 units, a 36% decrease compared to the same period.
You may also like
According to DXS-FERI, transactions are mainly concentrated in projects with favorable locations, complete legal documentation, reputable developers, and meeting the needs of actual residents. Short-term speculation remains limited, while buyers are more cautious before taking out long-term loans.
The cost of home loans is a major obstacle for buyers. In the third quarter, fixed interest rates for the first 12 months were commonly between 8.5% and 11.5% per year. After the preferential period, floating interest rates ranged from 13% to 15% per year. The pressure of interest payments caused many customers to delay their decision before purchasing.
Offer discounts and flexible payment options to attract customers.
According to a survey by DXS-FERI, real estate prices in Q3 2026 generally decreased by 5-20% compared to Q2. The decrease varied between regions and property types, with the North recording the most significant adjustments.
In the apartment segment, selling prices in the North decreased by 15-20%, ranging from 45-160 million VND/m². In the Central region, prices decreased by 10-15%, with prices from 30-100 million VND/m². In the South, mainly Ho Chi Minh City and Dong Nai City, along with the Mekong Delta, prices decreased by 5-10%. Apartment prices in these two areas ranged from 36-145 million VND/m² and 30-55 million VND/m² respectively.
For low-rise houses in urban areas, selling prices in the North decreased by 15-20%, ranging from 70-280 million VND/m². In the South, prices decreased by 10-15%, with prices ranging from 50-320 million VND/m². The Central and Western regions also saw a 10-15% decrease, with selling prices ranging from 45-200 million VND/m² and 30-100 million VND/m² respectively.
Land prices decreased in all four regions. The North recorded the sharpest decline, with selling prices ranging from 45 to 90 million VND/m². The South, Central, and Western regions all saw decreases of 10-15%; selling prices ranged from 25-135 million VND/m², 15-75 million VND/m², and 10-40 million VND/m² respectively.
To improve sales, developers combine price reductions with discounts, extended payment schedules, interest rate support, and principal repayment grace periods of 2-5 years. Some projects offer payment plans of around 6-8 million VND/month to reduce the amount customers have to spend in the initial phase.
You may also like
Project implementation activities continue. In the first three quarters of the year, DXS-FERI recorded 39 project commencements, 93 business launch events, and 54 sales launch events. In the third quarter alone, there were 8 project commencements and 12 sales launch events. According to the report, the company is being more cautious when bringing products to market.
DXS-FERI forecasts that approximately 30,300 new products will be added in Q4/2026, bringing the total primary supply for the year to over 140,000 products. The South, mainly Ho Chi Minh City and Dong Nai City, is expected to account for about 56% of the new supply in the last quarter of the year.
According to forecasts, selling prices in the fourth quarter may remain around the third quarter level, with a supply-to-demand absorption rate of approximately 30-35%. The potential for improved transactions continues to depend on interest rates and actual purchasing power. Projects with transparent legal status, reasonable prices, and suitable payment policies are expected to have an advantage in attracting buyers.

articles.title: Institutional launching pad for the FDI economic sector. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Institutional launching pad for the FDI economic sector.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
4 major pillars of reform
Institutional launching pad for the FDI economic sector.
(DTTC) - The draft Law amending and supplementing a number of articles of the Investment Law is currently being reviewed by the Ministry of Justice; it is expected to be submitted to the 16th National Assembly for consideration and approval at its second session in October 2026. These amendments aim to comprehensively institutionalize Resolution 10-NQ/TW dated June 8, 2026, of the Politburo on the development of the economy with foreign direct investment (FDI).
To date, although the FDI sector has become a crucial driver of export growth and contributed to job creation, its isolated operation persists. This includes the lack of organic integration between multinational corporations and the domestic private sector, resulting in modest domestic value added. Furthermore, there are constant risks of transfer pricing, tax evasion, the adoption of low-quality technologies, and negative impacts on resources and the environment.
Set against the backdrop of global geopolitical fragmentation and the profound restructuring of high-tech supply chains, Resolution 10-NQ/TW established a fundamental shift in the guiding principles. The draft Law amending and supplementing certain articles of the Investment Law reflects an effort to codify strategic orientations into normative regulations, focusing on four major pillars of reform.
Firstly, it is proposed to apply a special investment procedure (fast-track) for strategic technologies to projects in industrial parks, export processing zones, high-tech zones, digital technology zones, free trade zones, international financial centers, or strategic technology projects such as semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), and data centers.
Secondly, the draft proposes output-based incentives and the legalization of an Investment Support Fund. Specifically, the draft affirms the principle of time-limited incentives linked to the fulfillment of commitments on research and development (R&D), technology transfer, and localization. The State will directly finance the costs of human resource training, R&D, and supplier development. In addition, the draft officially legalizes the establishment of an Investment Support Fund to proactively respond to the Global Minimum Tax.
Thirdly, the proposal suggests allowing provincial People's Councils to use local budgets to directly support labor training costs for FDI enterprises, removing the barriers of the State Budget Law; allowing the application of accelerated depreciation policies for equipment and extending the term of ecological industrial park infrastructure projects up to 70 years.
Fourth, we propose establishing a National Investment Single Window and an independent transfer pricing assessment mechanism. The National Investment Single Window, chaired by the Ministry of Finance , would strictly adhere to the "one-time declaration, multiple-use" principle and process applications electronically throughout the entire process. Under this mechanism, state agencies would have the right to request independent assessments of the value of capital, machinery, and technology; investors would bear all assessment costs if found to have made false declarations that increase tax obligations or smuggled "technological waste" into Vietnam.
Strengthening the institutional launchpad
Despite proposing many progressive contents, compared to the requirements of Resolution 10-NQ/TW, the draft law still has some institutional gaps and the risk of dependence on specialized laws remains. Some current regulations in the draft only address general security principles, completely lacking a thorough national investment security review process. The concept of "ultimate beneficial owner" has not been clarified, leaving authorities without tools to prevent mergers and acquisitions (M&A) aimed at secretly acquiring data infrastructure through shell companies in "tax havens".
Another concerning gap is the lack of a testing framework (sandbox) for foreign indirect investment (FII), digital assets, and the expansion of foreign ownership limits to support the stock market upgrade. The draft adopts a safe solution by passively referencing the Securities Law, while the Securities Law does not directly regulate these matters, instead "pushing" them down to the decree level. The draft also lacks a framework to encourage Vietnamese experts and managers to start businesses after working at FDI corporations; it also lacks mechanisms for "seed capital," protection against non-compete clauses, and intellectual property transfer.
The fact that the National Assembly will consider and pass the Law amending and supplementing a number of articles of the Investment Law at its session in October 2026 is a very good opportunity to address gaps and strengthen the legal basis for investment activities in general and FDI in particular. For example, instead of passively referring to foreign entities, the new law should directly legalize the principle of expanding the foreign ownership limit for non-sensitive sectors, creating a sufficiently strong legal basis for the process of upgrading the market status.
The draft law amending and supplementing five laws, including the Labor Code, is also included in the legislative program for October 2026. This creates favorable conditions for immediately including a provision to completely exempt technology experts in strategic technology categories from work permits. In addition, regulations on entry and exit should include a "Technology Talent Visa" with a 5-10 year term, integrating family sponsorship and home ownership rights to create a superior attraction for top scientists and technology experts.

articles.title: From raw ore to EV power: Indonesias US$10 bln nickel transformation - ANTARA News
articles.summary: From raw ore to EV power: Indonesias US$10 bln nickel transformation  ANTARA News
articles.full_text:
President Prabowo Subianto delivers his remarks prior to launching several downstreaming projects at the Weda Bay Industrial Park in Central Halmahera, North Maluku, on Thursday (October 8, 2026). (ANTARA FOTO/Galih Pradipta/app/nz/am)
That sharp sound marked the moment a long-held vision broke out of planning documents and into reality. Electric vehicle (EV) batteries—manufactured in the heart of Indonesia’s nickel region—were officially shipped off to international markets.
President Prabowo Subianto himself activated the siren. With that simple gesture, he inaugurated the commercial operations of four major industrial projects and broke ground on seven new ones.
Together, these eleven ventures represent a combined investment value of US$10.2 billion.
While the total investment amount is massive, the strategic nature of the projects carries even greater weight. The four facilities entering full commercial operations are Blue Sparking Energy, REPT Battero Indonesia, Pioneer Aluminium Industries and XCMG Indonesia Manufacturing.
Meanwhile, the seven facilities entering construction focus on nickel-based battery materials, separators, electrolytes, electrolytic aluminum, electric trucks for industrial use and photovoltaic glass for solar panels.
Taken together, these facilities establish an almost complete production chain—stretching from raw battery chemicals to the final electric vehicles that run on them.
The full impact of the event at Weda Bay becomes clear when looking back at recent history.
Before the nationwide nickel ore export ban took effect in 2020, Indonesia sold most of its mineral wealth abroad as raw earth. Data from the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources shows that export revenue from nickel and its derivatives stood at just US$3.3 billion in2017.
By 2024, that figure skyrocketed to US$33.9 billion, marking a more than tenfold rise for a nation that controls roughly 42 percent of global nickel reserves.
This massive transformation did not happen overnight. The initial phase focused on building domestic smelters to process raw ore into ferronickel and nickel pig iron for global stainless steel production.
The second phase moved into intermediate goods, such as nickel matte, mixed hydroxide precipitate, nickel sulfate and cobalt—which now power the substantial trade surplus in North Maluku province.
The third and final phase turns those intermediate products into complete battery components. Batteries represent the final step before assembling the electric vehicles themselves.
Each step up this ladder fundamentally changes the nature of what Indonesia sells to the world.
Raw ore is traded strictly on tonnage and grade, with prices set by international metal exchanges.
Advanced batteries, however, are sold on technical specifications: energy density, cycle life, safety features and the trust of global vehicle manufacturers.
At this advanced manufacturing stage, product pricing depends less on volatile commodity price swings and more on technology and industrial reputation. This shift in bargaining power forms the true core of Indonesia’s economic downstreaming policy.
Projects focused on battery separators and electrolytes fill a critical gap that previously left Indonesia’s battery ambitions incomplete.
Investment and Downstreaming Minister Rosan Roeslani noted that these facilities represent the nation's first separator plants.
Although smaller in physical scale than massive smelters, battery cells cannot function without them.
Rosan stressed that building a complete ecosystem—including end-of-life battery recycling—positions Indonesia firmly inside the global supply chain, rather than on its outer edges.
Heading to East
This rapid industrial growth is reshaping the economy of Eastern Indonesia, most visibly in North Maluku.
The province recorded the nation's highest economic growth rate in 2025 at 34.17 percent. It continued to lead the country in the second quarter of 2026 with a year-on-year growth rate of 15.35 percent.
Statistics Indonesia identified mineral processing as the principal engine behind these numbers, with Rosan adding that the processing industry now accounts for nearly half of the province's GDP.
The national economic picture reflects the same structural shift. The contribution of downstreaming projects to total national investment rose from 25 percent to 35 percent over the last two years, with more than 75 percent of those funds spent outside Java.
Indonesia’s economy, long concentrated on Java, is steadily moving its economic center toward the east, with Weda Bay serving as the clearest example.
Since 2018, the Weda Bay industrial zone has drawn roughly US$20 billion in investment, with another US$7 billion planned to bring the total to US$27 billion.
Fifty-two international companies, including global traders Glencore and Trafigura, operate within the park and employ a workforce of 117,000 people.
The industrial park generates US$11 billion in exports. Combined with the Morowali Industrial Park in Central Sulawesi, total exports reach US$28 billion, accounting for about 10 percent of Indonesia's national export earnings.
Two remote island industrial zones now deliver one-tenth of the nation's export revenue.
However, rapid expansion presents its own set of long-term economic questions. North Maluku Governor Sherly Tjoanda warned that such intense growth requires careful oversight because the local economy relies heavily on finite mineral extraction.
Her warning outlines a clear roadmap for policymakers. The best defense against over-reliance on raw mining is to move continuously higher up the industrial value chain.
As production extends further away from the mine pit, a larger share of economic value comes from human skills, advanced machinery and proprietary technology—assets that remain valuable long after underground reserves run dry.
Social development is also expanding alongside industrial output. Corporate social responsibility programs across the area now reach 32 local villages, supported by funding that exceeds Rp650 billion (approximately US$36.52 million). President Prabowo emphasized that industrial operators must continue actively supporting local communities.
Serving domestic market
Among the new groundbreakings, the photovoltaic glass plant holds particular strategic importance. This facility directly supports the 100-gigawatt-peak solar power initiative launched by the President in Gilimanuk, Bali, last August.
That three-year national energy project requires an estimated investment of Rp1,140 trillion (US$64.04 billion). Rosan confirmed that Tsingshan, the main developer of Weda Bay, has opened discussions with state investment body Danantara to participate in the solar plan.
Downstreaming at Weda Bay is moving beyond overseas exports to supply Indonesia's own domestic energy transition.
The industrial complex now produces solar panel glass, energy storage batteries and heavy electric trucks to replace diesel vehicles inside mining sites.
Industrial complexes that supply national clean energy needs build stronger insulation against international market swings.
President Prabowo noted that these achievements build upon decisions made by previous presidential administrations—forming part of a continuous national effort.
His statement highlights that effective industrial policy demands a timeline far longer than a single political term.
Indonesia's nickel strategy has navigated trade disputes at the World Trade Organization, commodity market swings and political transitions without losing focus.
That policy consistency gives international investors the confidence to fund projects that require over a decade to recoup their initial capital.
The initial shipment of battery components from Weda Bay marks a major turning point.
Indonesia has reached the top rung of the industrial downstreaming ladder.
The immediate priority moving forward is to ensure that national engineers, local businesses and researchers climb that same ladder—keeping the value created firmly inside the country.

articles.title: Japanese FDI capital is driving green transformation in Vietnamese industrial production. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Japanese FDI capital is driving green transformation in Vietnamese industrial production.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
In particular, investments from FDI capital flows reflect the long-term vision and confidence of Japanese businesses in the potential for sustainable economic growth in Vietnam and the region.
Highlights of investment cooperation
In fact, a bright spot in Vietnam-Japan economic relations has been investment cooperation, a prime example over the past several years. According to statistics from the Trade Promotion Agency of the Ministry of Industry and Trade , Japan has over 5,800 active projects in Vietnam with a total investment capital exceeding US$81 billion. Simultaneously, numerous Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) continue to facilitate businesses in both countries in terms of tariffs, rules of origin, and trade facilitation, expanding opportunities for deeper participation in regional supply chains and production networks.
Khám phá thêm
Tìm hiểu lịch sử
Đọc Mẹo Du Lịch
Khám phá ĐNA
In particular, a number of Japanese corporations and businesses are not only committed to but also continuously expanding their production in Vietnam, such as Honda, Panasonic, Kao Vietnam, Sumitomo, etc. Meanwhile, a new wave of investment from Japanese businesses is continuously flowing into Vietnamese industrial parks, contributing to promoting green transformation in production in line with sustainable development trends, with solutions that meet market demands and can adapt to new requirements.
For example, OJI Group, Japan, recently commenced construction of a new aseptic carton packaging plant in Vietnam under the Oji Liquid Pak (OLP) brand, with a total investment of US$110 million, at the Long Thanh High-Tech Park, Dong Nai province. The project demonstrates Oji Liquid Pak's long-term investment commitment in Vietnam, while also affirming Vietnam's strategic role as a manufacturing and supply hub in the Group's growth strategy in Southeast Asia, contributing to the region's shift towards circular packaging solutions and meeting policy requirements.
Mr. Nguyen Quoc An, Deputy Head of the Management Board of Industrial Parks and Economic Zones of Dong Nai City (DNIEZA), stated that large-scale projects like these not only contribute to promoting the development of the local industry but also create opportunities to enhance domestic production capacity and strengthen Vietnam's participation in the regional supply chain. The Management Board of Industrial Parks and Economic Zones of Dong Nai City commits to continuing to support and facilitate investors throughout the project implementation process, within its assigned functions, duties, and authority; promptly guiding and coordinating the resolution of any difficulties and obstacles that arise so that the project is implemented in accordance with regulations and can commence operations as soon as possible.
Mr. Kestutis Sliuzas, General Director of Oji Liquid Pak, shared that more and more manufacturing industries, including the packaging industry, are shifting to a new standard where efficiency, food safety, operational flexibility, and circular economy elements must go hand in hand. Therefore, the Oji Liquid Pak Co., Ltd. factory project combines the production of packaging for the food industry with research and development, technical services, installation, and maintenance of Japanese-made machinery, thereby contributing to the goal of creating a modern, high-quality, and high-value-added production environment in the industrial park.
You may also like
According to some experts, besides manufacturing, Japanese FDI flows into diverse fields such as research and development in natural sciences; repair, maintenance, and installation of machinery and equipment; and import, export, and distribution of goods in accordance with Vietnamese law . These are areas that have a positive impact on the development orientation of Vietnamese industrial parks in the current period.
Mr. Tran Viet Ha, Deputy Head of the Ho Chi Minh City Export Processing Zones and Industrial Parks Management Board (HEPZA), stated that facilitating investors' early project implementation after registration and reducing procedures related to planning and construction are the goals that HEPZA is focusing on currently and in the near future. Specifically, HEPZA will directly handle issues within its jurisdiction, while inter-agency matters will be handled in coordination; simultaneously, the approach will shift from a centralized administrative procedure to continuous monitoring and management throughout the project implementation process, from investment preparation to operation.
On the other hand, Resolution No. 10-NQ/TW dated June 8, 2026, of the Politburo on the development of the foreign-invested economy also sets out an important policy direction, shifting the strategic focus of Vietnam's investment attraction from prioritizing the quantity of foreign investment to emphasizing quality, specifically investments that bring high technology, innovation, human resource development, and technology transfer. Vietnam is no longer a destination for simple assembly activities based on cheap labor, but is positioning itself as a center for high value-added, technology-based investment.
Corporate responsibility
Entering a new era, with a strong shift from attracting investment based on quantity to attracting selective investment, many industrial parks in localities such as Ho Chi Minh City, Dong Nai, etc., are prioritizing projects with advanced technology, high added value, efficient land use, environmental friendliness, and the ability to participate in and enhance the locality's position in domestic and global supply chains. In this orientation, many industrial parks also demonstrate a particularly important role in creating space to accommodate projects with high quality, advanced technology and management methods, especially those demonstrating corporate responsibility towards the environment and the community.
Regarding the Japanese business community in Vietnam, Mr. ONO Masuo, Consul General of Japan in Ho Chi Minh City, assessed that, along with production, the community contributions of Japanese businesses over the years have further deepened the relationship between Japan and Vietnam. A prime example is Kao Vietnam, a Japanese company, which has strived to improve hygiene, protect health, and enhance the quality of life in Vietnam through programs such as the "Kao Hygiene Development Program in Vietnam," implemented since 2018, in addition to its production and business activities.
Recently, Kao Vietnam Company initiated the "Healthcare Enhancement Program: Improving the Health of Female Workers in Industrial Zones." This program, implemented by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in collaboration with the United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women), government agencies, healthcare units, and workplace stakeholders, demonstrates Japanese businesses' proactive contribution to the local community and their role in addressing social issues in Vietnam.
Mr. ONO Masuo further informed that the Vietnamese government has set clear economic growth targets towards 2030, and the process of improving institutions and infrastructure is progressing steadily. In addition, the living conditions and working environment of the people are constantly changing, especially in ensuring the legitimate rights of workers.
You may also like
On the business side, Mr. Shintaro Yasue, General Director of Kao Vietnam, said that the company started operating in Vietnam in 1996 and 2026 marks Kao's 30th anniversary in this market. Throughout the past three decades, the company has continuously developed its production and business sustainably, adapting to the changes in Vietnamese society and people's lives.
Entering the next phase of its development, Kao Vietnam aims to continue delivering new value to consumers, not only through strengthening its brand and products, but also by promoting initiatives that contribute to solving social problems in Vietnam. This is also part of the company's long-term and sustainable development strategy, with a desire to find ways to enhance corporate responsibility and contribute more to the local community.
Particularly in a rapidly developing urban area like Ho Chi Minh City, a large number of women actively participate in the workforce and social activities. Therefore, by applying their experience, the manufacturing business community can develop diverse initiatives that contribute to improving the health and lives of working women in Vietnam, helping female workers feel secure and work effectively.

articles.title: Textile and garment businesses are worried about retaining orders. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Textile and garment businesses are worried about retaining orders.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Order pressure
Textile and garment businesses are worried about retaining orders.
As the year draws to a close, not all businesses have abundant orders. Therefore, many domestic textile and garment businesses are facing the dilemma of simultaneously retaining orders and customers while ensuring production efficiency.
According to representatives of the Vietnam Textile and Garment Association (Vitas), in the first nine months of 2026, textile and garment export turnover reached nearly 32 billion USD, an increase of 2.9% compared to the same period. However, businesses still face pressure on business efficiency due to low unit prices, small orders, and tight delivery times, while the costs of raw materials, logistics, and compliance are increasing, eroding profits. Therefore, securing orders does not mean businesses can rest easy; when it is difficult to increase selling prices, businesses have to reduce costs in production, transportation, and delivery.
Mr. Truong Van Cam, Vice President and General Secretary of Vitas, stated that Vietnamese textile and garment products are currently present in 137 countries and territories. The US continues to be a key market, accounting for approximately 40% of the market share, alongside traditional markets such as the EU, South Korea , Japan, China, ASEAN, and potential markets in Africa and the Middle East. Although the first nine months of 2026 recorded positive export results, Vietnamese textile and garment businesses still face many unpredictable market variables. In the final stretch of the year, the Vietnamese textile and garment industry faces the challenge of both maintaining orders and improving export efficiency amidst increasingly fierce international competition.
However, the overall export results do not mean that all businesses have a stable supply of goods in the last months of the year. Mr. Bach Thang Long - Deputy General Director of May 10 Corporation - JSC shared: Some units have orders fully booked until the end of the year, while others have only partially filled their production plans and must continue to seek customers in a cautious market environment. Currently, May 10 Corporation - JSC guarantees enough jobs for its employees until the end of November 2026. Meanwhile, at Southern Textile and Garment Corporation (VSC), the supply of goods is expected to be sufficient to maintain factory operations throughout the fourth quarter. For urgent orders, the company proactively arranges overtime for 2-3 days per week to ensure timely delivery.
Meanwhile, according to Mr. Nguyen Ba Khanh Tung, Deputy General Director of Hanosimex, the October plan has only reached about 70%, while November and December have only reached about 30%. The gap in orders is growing larger towards the end of the year, while customers are still hesitant to place large-scale orders. According to Mr. Tung, customers are actively researching prices but remain cautious when finalizing orders. Therefore, the outlook for orders in the fourth quarter remains uncertain, and the company has not received many clear signals for the end of the year.
Increased connectivity reduces costs.
Regarding the textile and garment industry's statistics for the first nine months of 2026, Mr. Vu Duc Giang, Chairman of Vitas, shared that the export results were achieved thanks to the industry's persistent implementation of three strategic pillars: diversifying markets, partners, and products; promoting the application of technology; and strengthening supply chain linkages, aiming to build a sustainable supply chain throughout the industry. Mr. Giang stated that the textile and garment industry is significantly impacted by logistics. Port congestion, container shortages, fluctuating shipping rates, or additional surcharges can all affect delivery schedules and order fulfillment capabilities. When customers split orders and request faster delivery, delays at any stage can increase costs.
According to Mr. Truong Van Cam, domestic logistics costs currently account for about 9-10% of the value of import and export goods in the textile and garment industry. With a profit margin of only about 3-5%, this cost has a significant impact. When it is difficult to increase selling prices to compensate, every expense incurred during transportation narrows the profit margin. Therefore, in the race to secure year-end orders, logistics is not simply about transporting goods from the factory to the port, but has become an integral part of the competitive landscape and customer retention strategy.
To reduce costs, improving the efficiency of connectivity and organizing logistics infrastructure is a crucial issue. Dr. Bui Ba Nghiem, a senior specialist at the Import-Export Department ( Ministry of Industry and Trade ), stated that logistics infrastructure needs to be organized according to each goods chain, from storage, sorting, and packaging to distribution and return. Efficiency lies not only in the scale of investment but also in the ability to deliver goods on time, ensuring quality at a reasonable cost. Building more warehouses, expanding ports, or increasing transportation capacity does not automatically mean a reduction in logistics costs if the links in the chain lack synchronized connectivity. For the textile and garment industry, priority should be given to directly connecting concentrated production areas, shortening the distance and time for transportation from factories to ports, organizing transportation routes effectively, reducing transshipment, and increasing the ability to consolidate goods to lower costs for businesses.
Mr. Cao Huu Hieu, General Director of Vinatex Vietnam Textile and Garment Group, stated that the market still faces many challenges from now until the end of the year. Cotton and fiber prices are fluctuating sharply; the VND/USD exchange rate is trending upwards; demand in major markets such as the US and EU is shrinking; and increased logistics and raw material costs are narrowing profit margins. In addition, there are stricter requirements regarding origin, trade defense regulations, and increased competitive pressure from Bangladesh, China , and other producing countries. Therefore, in the final stretch of the year, Vietnamese textile and garment businesses not only need more orders but also must improve the efficiency of each order.

articles.summary: Nirmala Sitharaman concludes successful visit to Singapore, focusing on strengthening investment and financial cooperation  India Shipping News
articles.full_text:
SINGAPORE: Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman concluded her official visit to Singapore from October 8 to 11, 2026, after a series of high-level bilateral engagements and meetings with leading global investors, financial institutions and businesses aimed at strengthening India–Singapore Economic and Financial Cooperation.
During the visit, the Union Finance Minister called on H.E. Mr. Tharman Shanmugaratnam, President of Singapore, and H.E. Mr. Lawrence Wong, Prime Minister of Singapore, and met H.E. Mr. Gan Kim Yong, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade & Industry, and H.E. Dr. Vivian Balakrishnan, Minister for Foreign Affairs.
The engagements provided an opportunity to review progress in advancing the outcomes of the 4th India–Singapore Ministerial Roundtable (ISMR) and explore avenues to further deepen the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The two sides also exchanged views on strengthening India–ASEAN cooperation and regional economic ties, including in the run-up to Singapore’s ASEAN Chairmanship in 2027.
Smt. Sitharaman also participated in a luncheon meeting hosted by H.E. Mr. Tharman Shanmugaratnam, President of Singapore, and Ms. Kristalina Georgieva, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The luncheon brought together senior leaders from global financial institutions, investment firms, academia and the Singapore Government, providing an opportunity for exchanges on global economic and financial developments.
Discussions with Singapore’s leadership focused on expanding bilateral investment, strengthening financial connectivity and advancing cooperation in emerging technologies. The Union Finance Minister highlighted India’s strong macroeconomic fundamentals, growth prospects and ongoing policy reforms, and encouraged greater investment by Singapore-based institutional investors and businesses in India’s growth story. Select infrastructure projects from the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) pipeline were highlighted for consideration by investors, with a view to facilitating follow-up discussions and engagement with relevant Indian authorities.
As part of the investment outreach, Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman participated in a business roundtable with senior representatives of leading global financial institutions and investment firms, including JPMorgan Chase, BlackRock, Deutsche Bank, PIMCO, the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), Carlyle, Temasek, Millennium Management, Citadel, and Brevan Howard. The discussions covered India’s continued commitment to economic reforms and resultant economic resilience amidst global uncertainties, developments in global and domestic financial markets, the implications of rapid advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), and opportunities to attract greater global capital into Indian assets. The participants expressed confidence in India’s growth story. They remarked that they look forward to continued progressive, fiscally prudent, predictable, growth-oriented policies of the government along with a focus on infrastructure.
The Union Finance Minister also held separate bilateral meetings with senior leadership of major institutional investors, financial institutions, and global corporations, including Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC), Wellington Management, Standard Chartered Bank, GIC (Government of Singapore Investment Corporation), DBS Bank, Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken (SEB), Temasek, TPG, HPS Investment Partners, CapitaLand Investment, Intel, British International Investment (BII), IHH Healthcare, and B Capital.
The senior leadership of these financial institutions and global corporations expressed strong investment interest in key sectors, including consumer markets, start-ups, FinTech, Deep-tech, and healthcare. These engagements also explored investment and financing opportunities across infrastructure, especially AI and AI related infrastructure including semiconductors and data centres, renewable energy for India’s energy transition and energy security, manufacturing, MSMEs and trade finance, financial services, food supply chains and other growth-oriented sectors.
Opportunities relating to aircraft leasing, treasury centres and greater participation by global investors in India’s financial markets were also explored. Mobilising long-term institutional capital and expanding avenues for financing India’s infrastructure and development priorities were key themes of the investment discussions. Smt. Sitharaman encouraged investors to explore opportunities through the NIIF and GIFT International Financial Services Centre (GIFT IFSC). The participants reaffirmed their strong commitment to the Indian market and expressed their intention to sustain and expand their investments in India, reflecting continued confidence in the country’s long-term growth prospects.
The visit also advanced dialogue on financial connectivity and emerging financial technologies. In meetings with Singapore’s financial authorities, including the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), both sides exchanged views on frontier technologies such as tokenisation of financial assets, digital money, central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), interoperability and trusted settlement arrangements. Singapore expressed its keenness to share its experience in asset tokenisation. The discussions provided an opportunity to explore further cooperation between the financial authorities of the two countries on emerging technologies and their application in financial markets.
Engagements with businesses also covered opportunities arising from India’s expanding semiconductor and AI ecosystems. Discussions included investment under the India Semiconductor Mission, development of skilled manpower, industry-linked training and AI skilling initiatives, and the application of AI in banking and financial services. Other areas included renewable energy, electric mobility, aviation maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), food security and processing, sustainable finance, and healthcare infrastructure.
Engagement with the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) focused on strengthening business-to-business linkages through targeted business matching and visits by Singapore business delegations to India for meaningful interactions with Indian businesses and State Governments. SBF highlighted potential areas for collaboration, including semiconductor supply chains, MRO, food security and food processing.
The visit reaffirmed the depth of the India–Singapore partnership and the shared interest in translating ongoing policy dialogue into greater investment, business engagement and financial cooperation. The wide-ranging interactions with Singapore’s political leadership, institutional investors, financial institutions and businesses helped showcase India’s growth and investment opportunities, identify areas of mutual interest and strengthen channels for follow-up engagement. The discussions are expected to support continued efforts to mobilise long-term capital, deepen financial connectivity and advance cooperation in emerging and strategic sectors.
Smt. Sitharaman was accompanied by the CEO of the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF), the Chairperson of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), and senior officials of the Department of Economic Affairs.
