articles.title: FM Sitharaman Holds Singapore Talks With Global Investors On India Financing - TradingView
articles.summary: FM Sitharaman Holds Singapore Talks With Global Investors On India Financing  TradingView
articles.full_text:
Meetings with SMBC, SEB, HPS Investment Partners, B Capital Group and MUFG focused on expanding financing and investment opportunities in India
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman held meetings with senior executives of five global financial institutions and investment firms in Singapore to discuss investment and financing opportunities in India across infrastructure, private credit, artificial intelligence (AI), renewable energy and housing finance.
According to posts shared by the Ministry of Finance on X, the meetings involved representatives from Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC), Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken (SEB), HPS Investment Partners, B Capital Group and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG).
During her meeting with HPS Investment Partners Chief Executive Officer Scott Kapnick, Sitharaman discussed private credit, structured finance and long-term financing for businesses.
According to the ministry, she encouraged HPS to explore setting up a fund in Gujarat International Finance Tec-City's International Financial Services Centre (GIFT IFSC) and collaborating with the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) to mobilise financing for large infrastructure projects in India.
HPS highlighted the potential for debt capital to complement equity investments, the ministry said.
Sitharaman's meeting with MUFG Chief Executive for Asia Pacific Yukinobu Saeki focused on expanding the bank's engagement in India across capital markets, infrastructure and project finance, renewable energy and mergers and acquisitions financing.
She also encouraged greater engagement with the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) to support infrastructure financing.
The discussions covered financing for Indian small and medium enterprises and regulatory roadshows aimed at enhancing market transparency and governance.
SEB Explores Investment Opportunities
During her meeting with SEB Chairperson Marcus Wallenberg, Sitharaman discussed India's economic outlook and ways to strengthen investment flows from European institutional investors.
According to the ministry, SEB highlighted opportunities in energy, data centres, information technology and tax services, healthcare, financial services and housing finance.
The discussions also covered sustainable finance, private equity investments in non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), the green transition and skill development.
Sitharaman met SMBC Managing Executive Officer and Co-Head for Asia Pacific Rajeev Kannan to discuss expanding the bank's activities in India.
The discussions included affordable housing finance, financing for NBFCs, trade finance and other priority sectors.
Sitharaman encouraged SMBC to explore investment and financing opportunities through NIIF and GIFT IFSC, particularly in aircraft leasing, according to the ministry.
B Capital Discusses AI Opportunities
Separately, Sitharaman met B Capital Group Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Raj Ganguly to discuss sovereign AI and the broader AI ecosystem.
She highlighted India's potential in AI services and encouraged the firm to explore applications of the technology in banking and financial services.
The ministry said B Capital emphasised the importance of a stable currency and predictable, transparent tax policies for investors.
The meetings focused on potential avenues to increase financing for Indian businesses and infrastructure and attract investment across technology, energy and other sectors. The ministry's posts did not specify any investment commitments or agreements arising from the discussions.

articles.title: Hon Hai Technology Group (Foxconn)'s Kathy Yang Honored In Most Powerful Women Asia 2026 By Fortune - Yahoo Finance Singapore
articles.summary: Hon Hai Technology Group (Foxconn)'s Kathy Yang Honored In Most Powerful Women Asia 2026 By Fortune  Yahoo Finance Singapore
articles.full_text:
Technology sector leadership showcases Asia's formidable strength
TAIPEI, Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Reflecting responsibilities that sit at the intersection of the physical industrial world and the AI world for the largest electronics manufacturer and AI server provider on the planet, Kathy Yang of Hon Hai Technology Group (Foxconn) (TWSE:2317) has been recognized in Most Powerful Women Asia 2026 by Fortune, for a second year.
As General Manager of Global Campus Operations and Head of AI Software Business and AI Infrastructure for Foxconn, Yang joins 16 honorees from technology, the most represented sector in this year's prestigious list, ahead of banking with 14. Their presence reflects the increasingly central role technology plays in Asia's economy, as businesses spanning digital platforms, advanced manufacturing and other technology-driven industries grow in scale and influence.
"What stands out in this year's ranking is how the landscape of business power in Asia is evolving," said Charmian Choo, Asia list Senior Manager. "We see established leaders continuing to shape some of the region's largest companies, alongside a new generation rising through the ranks. The prominence of technology is particularly striking, reflecting the sector's growing influence on Asia's economy and the women increasingly at the forefront of that transformation."
"Women in leadership play an important role in the AI industrial revolution. The real challenge is not deploying technology, but redesigning work, investing in reskilling, and helping our global talent of women and men evolve with it," said Foxconn's Yang, whose remit includes Foxconn's more than 240 sites across 24 countries. "Five years from now, the best factories will not simply be the most automated, but those where humans, AI and robots make one another better."
Earlier this year, Yang was recognized among Fortune's Most Powerful Women in Business 2026. Her work combines Foxconn's global manufacturing scale, engineering capabilities and operational know-how with software, data, computing infrastructure and AI.
Yang previously served as Foxconn's Rotating CEO, the first woman to hold the role, during which she focused on strengthening enterprise-wide execution, cross-business alignment, and governance discipline across one of the world's largest and most complex industrial organizations. She is concurrently a Board Director of Foxconn Industrial Internet (FII) and Chairwoman and CEO of JUSDA, both key units of Foxconn.

articles.title: From national resources to a prosperous Vietnam. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: From national resources to a prosperous Vietnam.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Vietnam is standing at a new threshold of development, with the aspiration to maintain high growth rates, aiming for double-digit growth and building a prosperous Vietnam. To go far on that journey, the country not only needs more resources, but must also transform those resources into tangible products, jobs, technology, and wealth.
Because when the economy cannot continue to grow indefinitely by simply adding more capital, more labor, or more projects, the deciding factor will be how much value is created by each dollar of capital, each inch of land, each grain of rice, and each hour of labor.
A prosperous Vietnam doesn't begin with GDP figures on paper. It begins with factories being built, roads being opened, Vietnamese products reaching the world , and, above all, technologies being mastered. At the heart of this flow are businesses and entrepreneurs – those who directly transform opportunities into products, capital into jobs, and ideas into value.
At the Government's Standing Committee meeting with the business community in July 2026, Prime Minister Le Minh Hung emphasized that the business community is "the pioneering force on the economic front, directly creating momentum for growth, employment, and enhancing national competitiveness ." In the goal of double-digit growth, the role of businesses therefore lies not only in capital size or the number of enterprises, but also in their ability to create new productivity, new added value, and new impetus for the economy.
At the Techcombank Investment Summit 2026, held on September 19th in Hanoi, the topic of infrastructure was presented within a broader context: it's not just about the structures built, but about the foundations that have the potential to open up new avenues for development.
According to Mr. Nguyen Xuan Bac, Deputy Director of the Department of Credit for Economic Sectors, State Bank of Vietnam, transportation infrastructure needs to be developed ahead of other sectors to open up new development opportunities, leading to increased trade and socio-economic growth. Besides essential infrastructure such as electricity, roads, schools, and hospitals, digital infrastructure is increasingly becoming a crucial component of the economy.
From the perspective of the Ministry of Construction , Mr. Nguyen Anh Dung - Deputy Director of the Planning and Finance Department, Ministry of Construction - believes that Vietnam is entering a phase of implementing exceptionally large-scale complex infrastructure projects such as high-speed railways, international airports, and urban development following the TOD (Transit-Oriented Development) model. These are no longer isolated projects but can form an entire ecosystem encompassing logistics, maintenance, commerce, real estate around the station, and many accompanying services.
For strategic infrastructure projects with significant spillover effects but low direct return on investment, Mr. Nguyen Anh Dung believes the State should maintain its leading role in public investment, creating "seed capital," combined with ODA and other preferential international funding sources. Conversely, for projects with good operational, exploitation, and return-on-investment potential, mechanisms should be in place to maximize private sector involvement.
Sharing the same perspective on resource diversification, Mr. Nguyen Xuan Bac emphasized that bank credit is an important source of capital but cannot be the sole source for large-scale infrastructure projects; it is necessary to mobilize resources synchronously from the State budget, bank capital, ODA, loans from international organizations and foreign investors.
The value of a project therefore lies not only in the project itself, but also in the economic activities it sparks: new logistics routes, new production areas, new capital flows, and new growth opportunities.
The higher the growth rate, the greater the demand for capital. Also at this event, Mr. Jens Lottner, CEO of Techcombank, stated that according to the bank's calculations, if Vietnam enters a GDP growth trajectory of 10%, the capital formation needs over the next five years could reach approximately US$1.1 trillion. Of this, infrastructure development and investments to support economic transformation alone could require around US$500 billion.
These figures show that banks cannot be expected to meet all of the economy's capital needs. Money for the economy must come from multiple sources: the State budget, bank credit, the stock market, corporate bonds, foreign investment, investment funds, and the capital of businesses themselves.
You may also like
Deputy Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam, Nguyen Ngoc Canh, emphasized the need for a more balanced development between the money market and the capital market, expanding channels for mobilizing medium and long-term capital, while ensuring market discipline and risk control.
When a business is large enough and transparent enough to enter the market, raising capital not only provides the business with additional resources for development but also encourages it to improve its governance standards, transparency, and competitiveness.
On September 21, 2026, the Vietnamese stock market was officially reclassified by FTSE Russell from a Frontier Market to a Secondary Emerging Market. This milestone opens up opportunities to access international capital flows, while also placing higher demands on transparency, governance, and corporate quality.
In just the first eight months of 2026, nearly 206,400 businesses were newly established or resumed operations. Of these, nearly 138,100 were newly established, with registered capital of nearly 1.71 trillion VND; the total additional registered capital injected into the economy reached nearly 4.4 trillion VND. Conversely, more than 40,800 businesses completed dissolution procedures, an increase of 125.5% compared to the same period.
These figures show that the problem for Vietnamese businesses is not just about how many more businesses there are, but how to ensure that businesses can stand firm, grow, increase productivity, and transform resources into value.
The story of Hoa Phat Group is a case in point. Driven by the demand from large-scale domestic construction projects, the company saw an opportunity to develop its steel production capacity, participate more deeply in industrial projects, and gradually elevate its position in the production chain.
Speaking about the opportunities presented by high-speed rail, Mr. Tran Dinh Long, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Hoa Phat Group, once emphasized: " If the Government does not give special priority, the opportunity will be missed."
What's noteworthy is not just about selling more products, but also about how businesses, driven by the country's needs, develop new production capabilities, master technology, and enhance the competitiveness of Vietnamese products.
That's also the challenge facing Vietnamese businesses today. They can't just grow in quantity. To go far, businesses must grow in technology, management, human resources, and the ability to participate more deeply in the supply chain.
Therefore, the target of 2 million operating businesses by 2030 will only be meaningful if, behind that number, there is a vibrant and highly competitive business community. To have large businesses, we must first have a continuously growing class of small and medium-sized enterprises.
Speaking at the 20th anniversary celebration of the Vietnam Association of Small and Medium Enterprises, Prime Minister Le Minh Hung affirmed: Small and medium enterprises must "become a solid foundation and a continuous source of replenishment for medium and large enterprises."
But businesses that want to grow cannot rely solely on capital. Capital can buy a factory, but it cannot immediately buy management capabilities. Money can buy machinery, but it cannot replace people who know how to master technology. Opportunities may arise, but businesses must have the capacity to turn them into results.
At Vingroup's 2026 Annual General Meeting, Mr. Pham Nhat Vuong, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Vingroup, spoke about the direction of renewable energy development: "Instead of discarding it, we need to utilize it to create value."
That's also a broader perspective on resources. Resources only have value when they are used; capital only truly has meaning when invested in the right place; technology only creates power when someone masters it. Resources are the starting point. Entrepreneurs are the ones who transform those resources into value.
As the economy grows, another thing happens: Private wealth accumulates. According to Knight Frank's Wealth Report 2026, Vietnam has approximately 1,233 individuals with a net worth of $30 million or more, and this number is projected to increase to around 1,960 by 2031.
You may also like
Those numbers don't just tell the story of those who got rich. They raise another question: what will be passed on to future generations?
A factory can be inherited. A piece of land, a portfolio of assets can be transferred. But the ability to create assets cannot be transferred.
The next generation may inherit a large business, but to maintain and grow it, they must learn how to manage during difficult times, innovate as the market changes, uphold business ethics, and understand the company's responsibility to the community.
That's also why today's entrepreneurial story isn't just about getting rich. It's about how to create wealth, how to preserve it, and what to leave behind for future generations.
A generation can pave roads, build bridges, construct factories, and create great enterprises. But a country only truly prospers when the next generation not only inherits what their ancestors left behind, but also has the capacity to make it better, bigger, and more beneficial.

articles.title: Woman throws 3 flower pots and rack from HDB block after night of drinking, jailed 4 weeks, Singapore News - AsiaOne
articles.summary: Woman throws 3 flower pots and rack from HDB block after night of drinking, jailed 4 weeks, Singapore News  AsiaOne
articles.full_text:
A 24-year-old woman who threw three flower pots and a rack from the corridor of an HDB block after a night of drinking was sentenced to four weeks' jail.
Melissa Rosabelle Misson was also fined $600 and disqualified from holding or obtaining all classes of driving licences for two years, reported Stomp on Sunday (Oct 11).
She faced four charges, including committing a rash act that endangered the life or personal safety of others, riding a motorcycle without a valid licence, and offences under the Liquor Control (Supply and Consumption) Act.
Misson pleaded guilty to one charge, while the remaining charges were taken into consideration during sentencing.
Spent night drinking at Clarke Quay
According to Shin Min Daily News, she had dinner with a group of friends near Clarke Quay at about 11.30pm on Oct 5, 2024, where she drank a pint of beer.
The group subsequently went to a nightclub, where she consumed another pint of beer and three whisky-based drinks.
At about 4.30am the following day, Misson followed a male friend to his home to spend the night there as she was heavily intoxicated and did not have her keys with her.
However, she insisted on leaving shortly after arriving. Concerned for her safety, her friend accompanied her outside.
He later heard her telling someone over the phone about her location in real time. Believing that someone was coming to pick her up, he returned home.
At about 6.15am, Misson was heard shouting a man's name outside a second-floor HDB unit and banging on its window.
She then threw three flower pots and a rack down from the corridor.
A 26-year-old male resident heard the commotion and opened his door to investigate and saw Misson throwing the items and shouted at her to stop.
Misson claimed she was looking for a man named Rizmi, but the resident told her that no one by that name lived there.
The resident's father subsequently called the police, and Misson was arrested.
A breath or blood alcohol test found that her blood alcohol concentration was 168mg per 100ml of blood.
In a separate incident on Sept 5, 2025, at about 2.40am, a traffic police officer caught Misson riding a motorcycle rented by a friend despite not holding a valid driving licence.

articles.title: Critically ill foreign sailor rescued by Vietnamese maritime team - Tuoi Tre News | The News Gateway to Vietnam
articles.summary: Critically ill foreign sailor rescued by Vietnamese maritime team  Tuoi Tre News | The News Gateway to Vietnam

source_detail.name: Tuoi Tre News | The News Gateway to Vietnam

articles.full_text:
The Vietnam Maritime Search and Rescue Coordination Center, under the Vietnam Maritime and Waterway Administration, confirmed on Sunday that it had launched an emergency rescue operation for a foreign crew member who fell seriously ill aboard the Marshall Islands-flagged cargo ship RAMHAN.
According to the ship’s captain, Panjanathan Elanchezhiyan, born in 1993 and serving as a third engineer, developed a series of alarming symptoms, including alternating fever and chills, dizziness, elevated blood pressure and impaired behavioural control.
Recognizing the seriousness of the situation, the captain issued an urgent request for medical assistance, according to the Vietnam Government Portal.
Upon receiving the distress report, the center quickly activated its emergency response procedures.
The center also established medical consultations and provided instructions to the vessel on administering initial first aid.
However, the sailor’s condition continued to worsen, making it imperative to transfer him ashore for specialized medical care.
Under the direction of the administration, the center dispatched the dedicated search and rescue vessel SAR 273 from its standby station in the south-central province of Khanh Hoa Province at 8:48 am on Sunday.
Throughout the operation, the rescue team maintained close coordination with the RAMHAN and relevant authorities and agencies.
Efforts focused on ensuring the patient’s safety and minimizing the time required to bring him ashore.
At around 9:30 am, SAR 273 reached the cargo ship and its crew began providing initial medical assistance to the ailing seafarer.
After completing the necessary procedures, the rescue team safely evacuated him from the RAMHAN and transported him towards the mainland for handover to the relevant authorities.
At 10:54 am, the Vietnamese rescue ship arrived at a pier in Khanh Hoa’s Nha Trang.
The patient was rapidly taken to a hospital in the province for further examination and treatment.

articles.title: Singapore regulator sets AI rules for banks and insurers - FinanceX Magazine
articles.summary: Singapore regulator sets AI rules for banks and insurers  FinanceX Magazine
articles.full_text:
Singapore’s financial regulator has put banks and fintechs on a fixed timetable to get their AI risk controls in order. On 7 October 2026, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) issued its Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management, setting supervisory expectations for how financial institutions govern AI. The MAS AI guidelines take effect on 7 October 2027, with phased implementation allowed until 7 October 2028, giving firms a hard compliance horizon rather than an open-ended principle to aspire to.
What exactly has MAS asked firms to do?
The guidelines are structured around four areas. Boards and senior management must own AI oversight and fold it into existing risk frameworks. Firms must run AI risk management systems that include a live inventory of every AI use case and materiality assessments scored on impact, complexity and reliance. They must apply controls across the full AI life cycle, covering development, deployment and maintenance. And they must hold the capabilities and capacity, both skilled staff and resilient infrastructure, to run AI safely.
The rules are deliberately proportionate: a firm’s obligations scale with the size and nature of its AI use. They also reach beyond conventional models to generative AI and, notably, AI agents, the autonomous systems now entering trading, servicing and compliance workflows.
Why now, and what led here?
This is the end point of a multi-year process. MAS set out its FEAT principles (Fairness, Ethics, Accountability and Transparency) in 2018, published a generative AI risk framework through Project MindForge in late 2023, and ran a thematic review of major banks’ AI use in 2024. A consultation paper followed in November 2025, and in January 2026 the Infocomm Media Development Authority released a Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI, positioning Singapore among the first jurisdictions to address autonomous agents directly.
Independent legal analysis, including commentary from Hogan Lovells, reads the move as a shift from principles-based guidance to supervisory-ready expectations, meaning AI governance is now likely to surface in routine MAS inspections and thematic reviews rather than sitting as voluntary good practice.
How does this fit the global regulatory picture?
Singapore is not moving alone. Following MAS’ consultation, the Financial Stability Board consulted on sound practices for responsible AI adoption, signalling coordinated international direction. The contrast with the EU AI Act, which hard-codes high-risk classifications and prescriptive obligations, is instructive: MAS has opted for proportionality and outcomes over a fixed rulebook, betting that flexibility keeps innovation onshore while still tightening accountability.
Why This Matters to FinanceX Readers
For firms with Asia-Pacific operations, the clock has started: AI governance frameworks, use-case inventories and agent controls need to be defensible by October 2027. For everyone else, MAS is a leading indicator. Its proportionate, agent-aware model is the template other regulators are converging on, and the FSB’s parallel work suggests the direction of travel is now set. Compliance leaders and technology buyers should treat this as a preview of the questions their own supervisors will soon be asking.

articles.title: A review of economic news for the week of October 5-9. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: A review of economic news for the week of October 5-9.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Overview
 The Vietnamese stock market was officially upgraded in September, but the expected breakthrough has yet to occur.
 Following FTSE Russell's official upgrade from frontier market to secondary emerging market, contrary to many investors' expectations, the Vietnamese stock market has not seen significant changes. In fact, many stocks have continued to decline, and the VN-Index is currently falling.
 At the close of the last trading session of September (September 30th), the VN-Index fell 0.51%, or 9.11 points, to 1,768.62 points. Compared to just before its upgrade (September 18th), the VN-Index has fallen by more than 47 points, or nearly 2.6%. The majority of stocks on the electronic price board declined.
 In early October, the index continued to decline, with the VN-Index falling by more than 33 points in just the first 7 trading sessions of the month (up to October 9th) compared to the end of September. Notably, market liquidity in September remained low, down 15.12% compared to August and more than half of the average trading value of 28,900 billion VND/session in 2025.
 According to many experts, the following are the main reasons why the Vietnamese stock market has been sluggish after its upgrade:
 - Firstly, the positive news about the upgrade of the Vietnamese stock market was already absorbed by prices before the official announcement. A year before FTSE Russell began announcing the possibility of Vietnam being upgraded from a frontier market to a secondary emerging market, there had already been positive impacts on the stock market. Therefore, when the upgrade was officially implemented, there was little further impact. In addition, FTSE is implementing the inclusion of Vietnamese stocks in its indices in four phases, starting with a 10% weighting in September 2026 and gradually increasing to 100% in September 2027. More importantly, the upgrade improved investor sentiment regarding market prospects, meaning the market will have many opportunities to restructure portfolios in the coming months.
 - Secondly, the low market liquidity indicates that much capital remains on the sidelines. The main reason is that bank savings interest rates remain quite high, ranging from 5.0% to 7.0% per year, not to mention promotional programs that push interest rates up to 8.0% to 9.0%, strongly attracting capital from the public. In addition, lending rates of 10% to 12% per year encourage many businesses to increase fundraising from major shareholders. The flow of money into the stock market has contracted; with high interest rates, investors are more inclined to be defensive and preserve their capital rather than invest in stocks, which are considered a high-risk investment channel.
 Globally, as the US Federal Reserve (Fed) and other major central banks raise policy interest rates, and with many forecasts suggesting these agencies will continue to raise rates until the end of the year, the trend of net outflows by foreign investors in many emerging markets, including Vietnam, continues. According to statistics, from the beginning of the year to September 2026, foreign investors have withdrawn over $120 billion from South Korea, over $36 billion from Taiwan, over $25 billion from India , and approximately $3.6 billion from Vietnam, etc. Furthermore, on the global stock market, the top 10 AI stocks currently account for about 41% of the total market capitalization of the US stock market, equivalent to the concentration of technology stocks during the peak of the Dot-Com bubble in 2000. Global investment funds are adjusting their strategies to this trend. Meanwhile, the Vietnamese stock market still lacks technology and AI stocks, and is not yet attractive enough to strongly attract foreign capital.
 - Regarding the Vietnamese stock market itself, in order to shift the interest stemming from its upgrade into a genuine and sustainable capital flow, the market needs to continue improving accessibility, enhancing the quality of securities, increasing transparency, and improving corporate governance.
 From now until the end of the year, experts believe that the Vietnamese stock market will return to fundamental factors such as interest rates, third-quarter business results, valuations, and industry prospects to assess the market and maintain growth momentum, while the impact of the upgrade will need more time to be reflected in cash flow and valuation levels. In the long term, Vietnam still needs to demonstrate its ability to attract capital, maintain liquidity, improve the quality of listed companies, and continue to remove barriers faced by foreign investors to become an attractive destination.
 Specifically, Vietnam needs more large-scale enterprises in strategic sectors, aiming for approximately 15-20 companies with a market capitalization of over $2.5-3 billion and an average daily liquidity of around $15-20 million per stock. On a market-wide scale, to increase supply, Vietnam needs to aim for a market capitalization increase from approximately 65-70% of GDP currently to 100-120% of GDP during the 2026-2030 period, along with liquidity of around $1.5-2 billion per trading session.
 Summary of the domestic market for the week of October 5-9.
 In the foreign exchange market during the week of October 5-9, the central exchange rate was adjusted upwards by the State Bank of Vietnam for the first two days of the week before falling back down. At the close of trading on October 9, the central exchange rate was listed at 25,629 VND/USD, a decrease of 7 dong compared to the end of the previous week.
 The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) listed the USD buying rate at 24,398 VND/USD, 50 dong higher than the floor rate; meanwhile, the USD selling rate was listed at 26,860 VND/USD, 50 dong lower than the ceiling rate.
 The interbank exchange rate rose for the first two sessions of the week (October 5-9) before falling again. At the close of trading on October 9, the interbank exchange rate stood at 25,880 VND/USD, a sharp decrease of 103 dong compared to the end of the previous week.
 The exchange rate on the free market fluctuated upwards last week. At the close of trading on October 9th, the free market exchange rate increased by 120 VND on the buying side and 130 VND on the selling side compared to the end of the previous week, trading at 26,060 VND/USD and 26,170 VND/USD respectively.
 In the interbank money market during the week of October 5-9, interbank VND interest rates fluctuated sharply across all maturities from 1 month downwards, especially the overnight rate. At the close of trading on October 9, interbank VND interest rates were: overnight 4.50% (+1.70 percentage points); 1 week 5.15% (+1.65 percentage points); 2 weeks 4.00% (-1.00 percentage point); 1 month 5.20% (-1.10 percentage points).
 Interbank USD interest rates fluctuated slightly across all maturities, closing the trading session on Friday, October 9th, at: overnight 3.85% (unchanged); 1 week 3.89% (unchanged); 2 weeks 3.92% (-0.01 percentage points) and 1 month 4.01% (-0.02 percentage points).
 In the open market last week, through the collateralized lending channel, the State Bank of Vietnam offered 30,000 billion VND with maturities of 7 days, 14 days, 35 days, and 91 days, with interest rates maintained at 4.5%. As a result, 10,081.46 billion VND was successfully bid. During the week, 46,679.04 billion VND matured through the collateralized lending channel.
 The State Bank of Vietnam did not offer State Bank bills for auction during the week of October 5th - October 9th.
 Thus, last week, the State Bank of Vietnam withdrew a net amount of VND 36,597.58 billion from the market through the open market channel. There was VND 96,744.35 billion circulating in the collateralized lending channel.
 On October 7th, the State Treasury successfully auctioned 19,500 billion VND out of 21,500 billion VND of government bonds offered (a successful bid rate of 91%). Specifically, the entire 7,500 billion VND for 5-year bonds and the entire 12,000 billion VND for 10-year bonds were successfully auctioned. The 3-year bonds offered 500 billion VND, the 15-year bonds 1,000 billion VND, and the 30-year bonds 500 billion VND were also successfully auctioned, however, there were no successful bids for any of these three maturities. The winning interest rates for the 5-year bonds were 4.27% and for the 10-year bonds 4.43% (both unchanged from the previous auction).
 On October 14th, the State Treasury is expected to offer 17,000 billion VND of government bonds, including 500 billion VND for 3-year bonds, 6,000 billion VND for 5-year bonds, 9,000 billion VND for 10-year bonds, 1,000 billion VND for 15-year bonds, and 500 billion VND for 30-year bonds.
 The average trading value of Outright and Repos transactions in the secondary market last week reached VND 18,897 billion per session, a significant decrease compared to VND 24,485 billion per session the previous week. Government bond yields showed little fluctuation last week. At the close of trading on October 9th, government bond yields were trading around: 1 year 3.54% (unchanged); 2 years 3.64% (unchanged); 3 years 3.72% (unchanged); 5 years 4.29% (-0.01 percentage point); 7 years 4.34% (-0.001 percentage point); 10 years 4.47% (-0.003 percentage point); 15 years 4.57% (-0.01 percentage point); 30 years 4.73% (unchanged).
 The stock market during the week of October 5-9 saw gains in the first two sessions followed by declines in the remaining three. At the close of trading on October 9, the VN-Index stood at 1,735.09 points, a slight decrease of 2.62 points (-0.15%) compared to the previous week's closing price; the HNX-Index lost 5.15 points (-1.93%) to 261.60 points, and the UPCom-Index fell 1.69 points (-1.34%) to 124.24 points.
